title: Playing dances as a boy and the 10th Cavalry band
summary: He gains experience playing dances with older men, then enlists in the 10th Cavalry band, learning solo work from trumpeter Elmer Moore.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Well, when you took up a cornet, did you play in the dance band or the brass band?

Well, no. See, I started in a brass band. Well, I happened to be... What you would say happened to be fortunate that I had a good trumpet player that learned, but he let me out a reed. So then the older men used to get my mother and let me... had me to play dances with them. And they would give my mother 50 cents a night for this to have me to come. But they would see that I was... You know, with that horn. Yeah, all right. And that's where I got my experience from, which carried me into the army. Mm-hmm. See? So you were in the First World War then? That's right. See, I enlisted in the army. I was in the first band. It wasn't particularly examination in the past. It was examination to go in the 10th Calvary. I was in the 10th Calvary.
Did you play a bugle or anything there too? No, it was right on it as a trumpet player. Right on it as a trumpet player. With the band then?

It was right on it as a trumpet player. Mm-hmm. And then I got my further music knowledge there from a trumpet player by the name of Elmer Moore, who was a soulist. When I got there, the bandmaster put me on Elmer Moore, told me he wanted me to be Elmer Moore's second. That's whenever Elmer Moore, who was a chief trumpet player, couldn't make concerts and I had to play souls. I had to play those souls. Yeah, play souls. And that's where I got the part of knowing the technical part about knowing the souls. Now, this all happened all right until I come out of the army in 1919. And this is the part that leads up to my other life.
